proofs.proof_tex:
Order the coordinates as \((U,D)\). By definition,
\[
J=\operatorname{blockdiag}(MX,I_D),
\qquad
J^{\prime}v=0
\Longleftrightarrow
v_D=0\ \text{and}\ X^{\prime}Mv_U=0.                  \tag{1}
\]
All diagonal entries of \(M\) are positive by the positive-factor assumption, so \(M\) is invertible.

Multiplying the normalized time columns of \(X\) by \(-1\) turns \(X\) into the oriented incidence matrix of \(H_U\) with the time-\(1\) vertex column deleted. This invertible column operation does not change rank. The graph is connected: every \(g\in C\) is joined to time \(1\), and \(\infty\in C\) is joined to every time \(t\). Equivalently, if \(Xv=0\), the rows \((g,1)\) force every cohort coordinate of \(v\) to be zero, and the rows \((\infty,t)\), \(2\le t\le T\), then force every normalized time coordinate to be zero. Hence
\[
\operatorname{rank}(X)=|C|+T-1.                       \tag{2}
\]

The edge set
\[
\mathcal T_0=\{(g,1):g\in C\}\cup
\{(\infty,t):2\le t\le T\}
\]
has \(|C|+T-1\) edges, is connected, and has no cycle, so it is a spanning tree. Its non-tree edges are exactly \((g,t)\) with finite \(g\) and \(2\le t<g\). Their number is therefore
\[
|U|-(|C|+T-1)=|U|-|C|-T+1=q.                           \tag{3}
\]

For such an edge \(e=(g,t)\), put \(w_e=Mr_{e,U}\). Its four nonzero entries are \(+1,-1,-1,+1\) on \((g,1),(g,t),(\infty,1),(\infty,t)\). In \(X^{\prime}w_e\), the two contributions at each cohort vertex cancel and the two contributions at time \(t\) cancel. Thus \(X^{\prime}Mr_{e,U}=0\), and (1) gives \(r_e\in\ker(J^{\prime})\).

The coordinate of \(r_e\) at its own non-tree edge is \(-1/\mu_{gt}\ne0\), whereas every other fundamental-cycle column is zero there. Hence the \(q\) columns of \(R\) are linearly independent. Finally, (1)--(2) give
\[
\dim\ker(J^{\prime})
=(|U|+|D|)-\{(|C|+T-1)+|D|\}=q.                        \tag{4}
\]
The \(q\) independent columns of \(R\) lie in this \(q\)-dimensional kernel, proving
\[
\ker(J^{\prime})=\operatorname{col}(R),
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}(R)=q.
\]

Use the fixed-strata score Hilbert space with conditional components \(s_g\), \(\mathbb E_gs_g=0\), and norm \(\|s\|_2^2=\sum_gp_g\mathbb E_gs_g^2\). Its continuous mean-derivative map has blocks
\[
z_g(s)=\mathbb E_g[(Y_g-m_g)s_g].                      \tag{1}
\]
Continuity follows from Cauchy--Schwarz and the finite second moments implied by the finite-fourth-moment assumption.

First consider an actual submodel admitted by the definition of \(\mathcal T_P\). That definition imposes the explicit differentiable-mean convention
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\varepsilon}Y
=m+\varepsilon z(s)+o(\varepsilon)
=m_\eta(\eta_\varepsilon),
\qquad
\eta_\varepsilon=\eta+\varepsilon v+o(\varepsilon).    \tag{2}
\]
Differentiating the smooth chart in (2) gives \(z(s)=Jv\), and the weighted-cycle theorem yields \(R^{\prime}z(s)=0\). Thus moment differentiation is stipulated in the experiment; it is not inferred for an unbounded moment from quadratic-mean differentiability alone.

Conversely, fix \(s\in L_2^0(P)\) with \(R^{\prime}z(s)=0\). The weighted-cycle theorem and full column rank of \(J\) imply
\[
\ker(R^{\prime})=\operatorname{col}(J),
\qquad
z(s)=Jv                                                   \tag{3}
\]
for a unique vector \(v\).

For each cohort, define
\[
w_g^{(L)}=(Y_g-m_g)\mathbf 1\{\|Y_g-m_g\|_2\le L\},
\quad
u_g^{(L)}=w_g^{(L)}-\mathbb E_gw_g^{(L)},
\]
and \(C_g^{(L)}=\mathbb E_g[(Y_g-m_g)u_g^{(L)\prime}]\). Dominated convergence gives \(C_g^{(L)}\to\Sigma_g\). Since \(\Sigma_g\succ0\), choose finite \(L_g\) such that \(C_g:=C_g^{(L_g)}\) is invertible, and write \(u_g=u_g^{(L_g)}\). The vector \(u_g\) is bounded and centered.

Let
\[
s_g^{[\ell]}
=s_g\mathbf 1\{|s_g|\le\ell\}
-\mathbb E_g[s_g\mathbf 1\{|s_g|\le\ell\}]
\]
and correct its mean derivative by
\[
\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}
=s_g^{[\ell]}
+u_g^{\prime}C_g^{-1}\{z_g(s)-z_g(s^{[\ell]})\}.        \tag{4}
\]
Truncation gives \(s^{[\ell]}\to s\) in \(L_2(P)\), hence \(z(s^{[\ell]})\to z(s)\). By the definitions of \(u_g\) and \(C_g\),
\[
\mathbb E_g\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}=0,
\qquad
z_g(\widetilde s^{[\ell]})=z_g(s),                     \tag{5}
\]
and the correction in (4) tends to zero in \(L_2(P_g)\). Thus \(\widetilde s^{[\ell]}\to s\) in \(L_2(P)\), and every corrected score is bounded.

Smoothness of \(m_\eta\) and (3) imply
\[
r_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)
:=m_{\eta,g}(\eta+\varepsilon v)-m_g-\varepsilon z_g(s)
=O(\varepsilon^2).
\]
Set \(\lambda_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)=C_g^{-1}r_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)\) and define
\[
\frac{dP_{g,\varepsilon}^{[\ell]}}{dP_g}
=1+\varepsilon\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}
+u_g^{\prime}\lambda_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon).          \tag{6}
\]
The added terms in (6) have expectation zero, so this density integrates to one. Since \(\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}\) and \(u_g\) are bounded and \(\lambda_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^2)\), it is strictly positive for all sufficiently small positive and negative \(\varepsilon\). It therefore preserves support. Equations (5)--(6) give the exact mean
\[
\mathbb E_{P_{g,\varepsilon}^{[\ell]}}Y_g
=m_g+\varepsilon z_g(s)+C_g\lambda_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)
=m_{\eta,g}(\eta+\varepsilon v).                       \tag{7}
\]
Uniform Taylor expansion of the square root of the bounded positive density gives
\[
\left\|
\sqrt{\frac{dP_{g,\varepsilon}^{[\ell]}}{dP_g}}
-1-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}
\right\|_{L_2(P_g)}
=o(|\varepsilon|),                                     \tag{8}
\]
so (6) is differentiable in quadratic mean with score \(\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}\). For small \(\varepsilon\), its density is bounded above, so finite fourth moments are preserved. Covariances vary continuously and remain positive definite. Equation (7) remains in the positive rank-one mean chart. Consistency and no anticipation are retained by the same observed-law causal completion on the unobserved potential outcomes. Hence (6) is a two-sided support-preserving submodel in \(\mathcal M_4\).

Every \(s\) satisfying \(R^{\prime}z(s)=0\) is therefore the \(L_2(P)\) limit of bounded actual scores. The converse followed from (2). Since \(s\mapsto R^{\prime}z(s)\) is continuous, its kernel is closed, and
\[
\mathcal T_P=\{s\in L_2^0(P):R^{\prime}z(s)=0\}.
\]

First identify the causal target from the observed law. On \(U\), consistency and no anticipation imply
\[
\mathbb E_PY_{gt}=\mathbb E_PY_{gt}(0)=\mu_{gt}.
\]
On \(D\), consistency gives \(\mathbb E_PY_{gt}=\mathbb E_PY_{gt}(1)=\nu_{gt}\), while the rank-one untreated-mean assumption gives \(\mathbb E_PY_{gt}(0)=a_gb_t=\mu_{gt}\). Therefore
\[
A=\sum_{(g,t)\in D}p_g\mathbb E_PY_{gt}(1),
\qquad
B=\sum_{(g,t)\in D}p_g\mathbb E_PY_{gt}(0)>0,
\]
so the observed mean chart identifies the causal contrast \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}=A/B-1\).

The weighted-cycle theorem gives full column rank of \(J\). The covariance-interior and positive-share assumptions give \(\Omega\succ0\). Hence
\[
Q:=J^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}J\succ0.                        \tag{1}
\]
Along an admitted score \(s\), tangent-score density gives \(z(s)=Jv\), where \(v=\dot\eta_0\). Differentiating \(A/B-1\), using \(B>0\), yields
\[
\dot\theta_P(s)=c^{\prime}v.                            \tag{2}
\]

In the mixture representation, conditional on \(G=g\), the nonzero block of \(Z\) is \((Y_g-m_g)/p_g\). Hence
\[
\mathbb E_P[Zs]=z(s),
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[ZZ^{\prime}]=\Omega.                        \tag{3}
\]
For \(h^{\star}=\Omega^{-1}JQ^{-1}c\),
\[
J^{\prime}h^{\star}=c,
\qquad
\Omega h^{\star}=JQ^{-1}c.                              \tag{4}
\]
Combining (2)--(4), for every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[\phi^{\star}s]
=h^{\star\prime}z(s)
=h^{\star\prime}Jv
=c^{\prime}v
=\dot\theta_P(s).                                       \tag{5}
\]
Moreover, \(z(\phi^{\star})=\Omega h^{\star}=JQ^{-1}c\), so tangent-score density implies \(\phi^{\star}\in\mathcal T_P\). Thus (5) is the Riesz representation of the pathwise derivative in the tangent space, and
\[
\mathbb E_P[(\phi^{\star})^2]
=h^{\star\prime}\Omega h^{\star}
=c^{\prime}Q^{-1}c
=V^{\star}.                                             \tag{6}
\]
The cited regular-estimator information bound applies to this explicitly mean-differentiable differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment. Equations (5)--(6) therefore prove that \(\phi^{\star}\) is the canonical gradient and that every regular estimator has asymptotic variance at least \(V^{\star}\).

The weighted-cycle theorem gives \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=|C|+T-1\). Since every \(p_g\mu_{gt}>0\) on \(U\),
\[
S=X^{\prime}P_UMX\succ0.                                \tag{1}
\]
The fixed-strata central limit theorem gives \(\overline Y-m=O_P(N^{-1/2})\) and the stated Gaussian limit with covariance \(\Omega\). Also, \(\widehat p_g\to p_g\). Entrywise Chebyshev applied to \(Y_{gt}Y_{gs}\), whose second moment is finite under the fourth-moment assumption, gives \(\widehat\Sigma_g\to_P\Sigma_g\).

Because the finitely many untreated means are positive,
\[
\Pr\!\left\{\min_{(g,t)\in U}\overline Y_{gt}>0\right\}\to1. \tag{2}
\]
For positive sample cell means, the normalized PPML criterion has Hessian
\[
-X^{\prime}\widehat P_U
\operatorname{diag}\{\exp(X\beta)\}X\prec0.              \tag{3}
\]
It is coercive: along a nonzero ray, a positive component of the fitted log mean makes the negative exponential term diverge to \(-\infty\); if every component is nonpositive, full column rank supplies a negative component, and its strictly positive sample mean makes the linear term diverge to \(-\infty\). Thus the normalized solution exists uniquely on (2). Standard finite-dimensional local inversion gives consistency. Covariance consistency and continuity then imply \(\widehat K\to_PK\succ0\) when \(q>0\), and altogether
\[
\Pr(\mathcal E_N)\to1.                                  \tag{4}
\]

Expand the score at the true \(\beta\). For a point \(\widetilde\beta\) between \(\widehat\beta\) and \(\beta\),
\[
0=X^{\prime}\widehat P_U(\overline Y_U-\mu_U)
-X^{\prime}\widehat P_U
\operatorname{diag}\{\exp(X\widetilde\beta)\}X
(\widehat\beta-\beta).                                  \tag{5}
\]
The second matrix tends to \(S\), while
\[
X^{\prime}(\widehat P_U-P_U)(\overline Y_U-\mu_U)
=o_P(N^{-1/2})                                           \tag{6}
\]
because \(\widehat P_U-P_U=o(1)\) and \(\overline Y_U-\mu_U=O_P(N^{-1/2})\). Solving (5) gives
\[
\widehat\beta-\beta
=S^{-1}X^{\prime}P_U(\overline Y_U-\mu_U)
+o_P(N^{-1/2}).                                         \tag{7}
\]

The fixed-target-weight numerator obeys
\[
\widehat A-A
=\sum_{(g,t)\in D}p_g(\overline Y_{gt}-\nu_{gt}).        \tag{8}
\]
For \(d=\partial B/\partial\beta=\sum_Dp_g\mu_{gt}x_{gt}\),
\[
\widehat B-B
=d^{\prime}(\widehat\beta-\beta)+o_P(N^{-1/2}).          \tag{9}
\]
Since \(B>0\), the ratio expansion using (7)--(9) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}
&=c_\beta^{\prime}(\widehat\beta-\beta)
+\sum_{(g,t)\in D}\frac{p_g}{B}(\overline Y_{gt}-\nu_{gt})
+o_P(N^{-1/2})\\
&=h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}(\overline Y-m)+o_P(N^{-1/2}),
\end{aligned}                                           \tag{10}
\]
because \(h_{\mathrm{CM},U}=P_UXS^{-1}c_\beta\). Multiplication by \(\sqrt N\) proves the linearization, and the fixed-strata central limit theorem gives asymptotic variance \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\).

The definitions give \(J^{\prime}h^{\star}=c\) and
\(\Omega h^{\star}\in\operatorname{col}(J)\).  The same calculation as
in (1) of the attainment proof gives \(J^{\prime}h_{\mathrm{CM}}=c\).
Thus \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}-h^{\star}\in\ker(J^{\prime})
=\operatorname{col}(R)\), while
\(R^{\prime}\Omega h^{\star}=0\).  Writing
\(h_{\mathrm{CM}}-h^{\star}=R\gamma\) and multiplying by
\(R^{\prime}\Omega\) gives \(b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=K\gamma\).
Since \(K\succ0\), this proves the projection identity
\[
h^{\star}=h_{\mathrm{CM}}-RK^{-1}b_{\mathrm{cyc}}.       \tag{1}
\]
Since \(R\) has full column rank and \(K\succ0\),
\[
h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}
\Longleftrightarrow
b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=0.                                     \tag{2}
\]
For every untreated cell \((g,t)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}})_{gt}
&=\frac1{p_g}\sum_{s=1}^T
\operatorname{Cov}_P(Y_{gt},Y_{gs})h_{\mathrm{CM},gs}\\
&=\sum_{s=1}^T\operatorname{Cov}_P(Y_{gt},Y_{gs})
\alpha^{\mathrm{CM}}_{gs}
=\mu_{gt}F_{gt}.
\end{aligned}                                           \tag{3}
\]
Thus the component of \(b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=R^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\) associated with finite \(g\) and \(2\le t<g\) is
\[
(b_{\mathrm{cyc}})_{gt}
=F_{g1}-F_{gt}-F_{\infty1}+F_{\infty t}.                \tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) prove the stated equivalence.

For independence, fix \(m,p\) and, for each non-tree edge \(e=(g,t)\), perturb only the symmetric entries \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{gt},Y_{gg})\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{gg},Y_{gt})\) by \(x_e\). Period \(g\) is treated, so \(h_{\mathrm{CM},gg}=p_g/B\). Hence the untreated coordinate \((g,t)\) of \(\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\) changes by
\[
\frac{x_e}{p_g}h_{\mathrm{CM},gg}=\frac{x_e}{B}.         \tag{5}
\]
The corresponding treated-coordinate change is killed because \(R_D=0\). The non-tree coordinate \((g,t)\) occurs only in its own fundamental cycle, with coefficient \(-1/\mu_{gt}\). Therefore
\[
\Delta(b_{\mathrm{cyc}})_{hs}
=-\mathbf 1\{(h,s)=(g,t)\}\frac{x_{gt}}{B\mu_{gt}}.     \tag{6}
\]
Every diagonal entry in (6) is nonzero because \(B>0\) and \(\mu_{gt}>0\). The covariance-to-balance map has rank \(q\), proving that the \(q\) equations are linearly independent.

Fix \(m\) and \(q>0\). Since \(0<\tau_0<\min_{g,t}m_{gt}\),
\[
0<s^0_{gt}=\sqrt{\tau_0m_{gt}}<m_{gt}.                  \tag{1}
\]
For finite \(g\), the mass in the definition of \(P_\rho\) is positive when \(\sum_{t=2}^{g-1}|\rho_{gt}|<1\), and it sums to one because every Rademacher product \(e_te_g\) has zero uniform sum. Orthogonality of products on the hypercube gives
\[
\mathbb E_\rho\varepsilon_{gj}=0,\qquad
\mathbb E_\rho\varepsilon_{gj}^2=1,\qquad
\mathbb E_\rho(\varepsilon_{gt}\varepsilon_{gg})=\rho_{gt}
\quad(2\le t<g),                                       \tag{2}
\]
with all other distinct-coordinate covariances zero. Therefore \(Y_g=m_g+s_g^0\odot\varepsilon_g\) has mean \(m_g\), and its only off-diagonal covariances are
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{P_\rho}(Y_{gt},Y_{gg})
=s^0_{gt}s^0_{gg}\rho_{gt}=x_{gt}.                     \tag{3}
\]
Every hypercube vertex has positive mass. Thus, for nonzero \(v\), \(v^{\prime}\varepsilon_g\) is not constant on the support, so \(\operatorname{Var}(v^{\prime}Y_g)>0\); every covariance block is positive definite. Equation (1) makes every outcome strictly positive, and finite support gives boundedness and finite fourth moments. Complete potential outcomes by equality on \(U\), the observed treated outcome on \(D\), and deterministic \(\mu_{gt}\) for the missing untreated outcome on \(D\). This enforces consistency, no anticipation, and the rank-one untreated mean. Hence \(P_\rho\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\).

At \(\rho=0\), \(\Sigma_{g0}=\tau_0\operatorname{diag}(m_g)\). On \(U\),
\[
(\Omega(0)h_{\mathrm{CM}})_U
=\tau_0MXS^{-1}c_\beta\in\operatorname{col}(MX).        \tag{4}
\]
Because \(R^{\prime}J=0\) and \(R_D=0\), equation (4) gives \(b_{\mathrm{cyc}}(0)=0\). The perturbations (3) join an untreated coordinate to a treated coordinate, so they do not change the untreated--untreated block and
\[
K(x)=R^{\prime}\Omega(x)R=R^{\prime}\Omega(0)R=K_0.    \tag{5}
\]
The diagonal response (6) from the primitive-balance proof is exact, so
\[
b_{\mathrm{cyc}}(x)=-B^{-1}D_\mu^{-1}x.                \tag{6}
\]
Since \(\Omega(0)\succ0\) and \(R\) has full column rank, \(K_0\succ0\). Substitution into the cycle-loss definition yields
\[
\Gamma(x)
=B^{-2}x^{\prime}D_\mu^{-1}K_0^{-1}D_\mu^{-1}x>0       \tag{7}
\]
for every nonzero admissible \(x\).

Now let \(\|\Sigma-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathcal A}<\delta_0\). The Rayleigh quotient gives
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_g)
\ge\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{g0})
-\|\Sigma_g-\Sigma_{g0}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
>\lambda_0/2.                                           \tag{8}
\]
For completeness, let \(Q_g=\Sigma_g^{1/2}-\Sigma_{g0}^{1/2}\). It solves
\[
\Sigma_g^{1/2}Q_g+Q_g\Sigma_{g0}^{1/2}
=\Sigma_g-\Sigma_{g0}.
\]
The integral solution to this Sylvester equation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|Q_g\|_{\mathrm{op}}
&\le
\frac{\|\Sigma_g-\Sigma_{g0}\|_{\mathrm{op}}}
{\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_g)}
+\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{g0})}}\\
&<\frac{\delta_0}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}}.
\end{aligned}                                           \tag{9}
\]
Let \(\varepsilon_g\) have independent Rademacher coordinates and set \(Y_g=m_g+\Sigma_g^{1/2}\varepsilon_g\). Its covariance is \(\Sigma_g\). Since \(\|\varepsilon_g\|_2=\sqrt T\), equation (9) and the radius restriction imply, coordinatewise,
\[
Y_{gt}
\ge m_{gt}-s^0_{gt}-\sqrt T\|Q_g\|_{\mathrm{op}}
>d_0-\frac{\sqrt T\delta_0}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}}
>d_0/2>0.                                                \tag{10}
\]
This is a bounded nonnegative law with mean \(m\), and (8) gives covariance interior. The same causal completion applies. Therefore
\[
\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma_0,\delta_0)
\subset\mathcal L(m).                                   \tag{11}
\]

By construction, \(\Sigma(x_0)\) lies strictly inside the ball (11). Rank \(q>0\) of \(\mathcal L_m\) implies \(\|\mathcal L_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}>0\), and (6) with \(x_0\ne0\) gives \(\mathcal L_m(\Sigma(x_0))\ne0\). If \(\|\Sigma-\Sigma(x_0)\|_{\mathcal A}<\eta_0\), then the definition of \(\eta_0\) gives \(\|\Sigma-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathcal A}<\delta_0\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\mathcal L_m(\Sigma)\|_2
&\ge\|\mathcal L_m(\Sigma(x_0))\|_2
-\|\mathcal L_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\|\Sigma-\Sigma(x_0)\|_{\mathcal A}\\
&>\tfrac12\|\mathcal L_m(\Sigma(x_0))\|_2>0.
\end{aligned}                                           \tag{12}
\]
Equations (11)--(12) prove that the asserted ambient ball is realizable and has nonzero cycle imbalance. Since \(K\succ0\) at every covariance-interior law, \(\Gamma=b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}K^{-1}b_{\mathrm{cyc}}>0\) throughout that ball.

Fix \(m,p\). If \(q=0\), the weighted-cycle theorem gives \(\ker(J^{\prime})=\{0\}\). Since \(J^{\prime}h_{\mathrm{CM}}=c\), uniqueness of this solution and of the variance-minimizing solution gives \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}\) for every \(\Omega\succ0\). The PPML linearization and canonical-gradient theorem then imply efficiency at every fixed-mean law in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\).

Conversely, if \(q>0\), the realizable quadratic-loss theorem supplies an admissible nonzero \(x\) with \(P_\rho\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\) and
\[
\Gamma(x)
=B^{-2}x^{\prime}D_\mu^{-1}K_0^{-1}D_\mu^{-1}x>0.      \tag{1}
\]
At that law, the PPML variance exceeds \(V^{\star}\), so efficiency cannot hold for every legal bounded law. This proves the topological if and only if.

At an arbitrary covariance-interior law, primitive balance gives
\[
h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}
\Longleftrightarrow
b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\mathcal L_m(\Sigma)=0.                \tag{2}
\]
Thus the efficient covariance laws are exactly
\[
\mathcal L(m)\cap\ker(\mathcal L_m).                    \tag{3}
\]
The diagonal covariance response has entries \(-1/(B\mu_{gt})\), so \(\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal L_m)=q\). Inside the ambient realizable neighborhood around \(\Sigma_0\), (3) is therefore the intersection with a proper codimension-\(q\) linear subspace; the strict-loss ball around \(\Sigma(x_0)\) proves that its complement has realizable interior.

Finally, \(K\succ0\). The Rayleigh quotient for \(K^{-1}\) gives
\[
\frac{\|b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_2^2}{\lambda_{\max}(K)}
\le
b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}K^{-1}b_{\mathrm{cyc}}
\le
\frac{\|b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_2^2}{\lambda_{\min}(K)}.      \tag{4}
\]
The middle term is \(\Gamma\). The comparison with Ciani and Fisher uses no premise from that paper: the necessity, sufficiency, and codimension conclusions follow from (1)--(4) and the preceding proved nodes.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_4\). Entrywise Chebyshev for the empirical second moments gives \(\widehat\Sigma_g\to_P\Sigma_g\), while share convergence gives \(\widehat p_g\to p_g>0\). The PPML proof gives \(\widehat\beta\to_P\beta\). Since \(R\) has full column rank, \(\Omega\succ0\), and \(q\) is fixed,
\[
\widehat R\to_PR,\quad
\widehat\Omega\to_P\Omega,\quad
\widehat K\to_PK\succ0,\quad
\widehat h^{\star}\to_Ph^{\star}                       \tag{1}
\]
on events with probability tending to one. For \(q=0\), delete the empty cycle objects. Since \(\Pr(\mathcal E_N)\to1\), the fallback is asymptotically irrelevant. Continuity in (1) gives
\[
\widehat V
=\widehat h^{\star\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat h^{\star}
\to_P
h^{\star\prime}\Omega h^{\star}
=V^{\star}.                                             \tag{2}
\]

The treated support is nonempty and \(p_g/B>0\) on \(D\), so \(c\ne0\). Since \(J^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}J\succ0\), this implies \(V^{\star}>0\). Efficient attainment and the fixed-strata central limit theorem give
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,V^{\star}).                     \tag{3}
\]
By (2), \(\sqrt{\widehat V/V^{\star}}=1+o_P(1)\).  Multiplying the
left side of (3), standardized by \(\sqrt{V^{\star}}\), by the factor
\(\sqrt{V^{\star}/\widehat V}=1+o_P(1)\) changes it by \(o_P(1)\).
Therefore
\[
\frac{\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})}
{\sqrt{\widehat V}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).                             \tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), continuity of the standard normal distribution at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) gives
\[
\Pr_P\!\left\{
\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\in
\left[
\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}\pm
z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V/N}
\right]
\right\}
\to1-\alpha.
\]
All limits are pointwise at the fixed \(P\); no uniform tail claim is used.

When \(q=0\), \(R\) has no columns. The variance projection therefore gives \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}\), the estimator definition makes no correction, and the empty quadratic form gives \(\Gamma=0\).

Let \(C=\{2,\infty\}\). There are \(1+T\) untreated edges, so
\[
q=(T+1)-2-T+1=0.                                       \tag{1}
\]
The untreated graph is the canonical tree. On \(\mathcal E_N\), \(X\) is square and nonsingular and \(\widehat P_U\) is diagonal positive. Hence the PPML score implies
\[
\overline Y_U=\exp(X\widehat\beta).                     \tag{2}
\]
Under \(\widehat b_1=1\), equation (2) gives
\[
\widehat a_2=\overline Y_{21},\qquad
\widehat a_\infty=\overline Y_{\infty1},\qquad
\widehat b_t=
\frac{\overline Y_{\infty t}}{\overline Y_{\infty1}}
\quad(2\le t\le T).                                     \tag{3}
\]
Only cohort \(2\) is treated, at periods \(2,\ldots,T\). Thus
\[
\widehat A=p_2\sum_{t=2}^T\overline Y_{2t},
\qquad
\widehat B
=p_2\overline Y_{21}
\sum_{t=2}^T
\frac{\overline Y_{\infty t}}{\overline Y_{\infty1}}.  \tag{4}
\]
The denominator is positive on \(\mathcal E_N\). Cancelling \(p_2>0\) in (4) gives the claimed explicit ratio, and the empty correction gives \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\).

Use the stacking
\[
U=((2,1),(3,1),(3,2),(\infty,1),(\infty,2),(\infty,3)),
\quad
D=((2,2),(2,3),(3,3)).                                  \tag{1}
\]
The smallest observed mean is \(1\). Cohorts \(2\) and \(\infty\) have noise magnitude \(1/10\), and every coordinate of cohort \(3\)'s noise has magnitude at most \(3/20\). Thus every realized outcome is at least \(17/20>0\).

The totals are
\[
A=\frac13\left(3+\frac92+\frac92\right)=4,\qquad
B=\frac13(2+3+3)=\frac83,\qquad
\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}=\frac12.                          \tag{2}
\]
There are six untreated edges and six vertices, so \(q=1\). Direct substitution into the cycle and PPML definitions gives
\[
R=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1&-1/2&-1&1/2&0&0&0&0
\end{pmatrix}^{\prime},
\]
\[
h_{\mathrm{CM}}=
\begin{pmatrix}
-15/16&3/16&-3/8&3/4&3/16&-3/8&1/8&1/8&1/8
\end{pmatrix}^{\prime}.                                 \tag{3}
\]
For \(g=2,\infty\), \(\Sigma_g=I_3/100\). In cohort \(3\),
\[
\Sigma_3=\frac1{400}I_3+vv^{\prime},
\qquad
v=\begin{pmatrix}1/10&-1/10&1/10\end{pmatrix}^{\prime}. \tag{4}
\]
Its eigenvalues are \(1/400,1/400,13/400\), so covariance interior holds. With
\[
\Omega
=\Pi\operatorname{blockdiag}(3\Sigma_2,3\Sigma_3,3\Sigma_\infty)
\Pi^{\prime},
\]
exact multiplication gives
\[
b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\frac9{640},
\qquad
K=\frac{183}{1600},                                     \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
h^{\star}
=h_{\mathrm{CM}}-R\frac{b_{\mathrm{cyc}}}{K}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
-15/16&63/976&-153/488&213/244&123/976&-3/8&1/8&1/8&1/8
\end{pmatrix}^{\prime}.                                 \tag{6}
\]
Consequently,
\[
h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}
=\frac{6663}{102400},
\qquad
h^{\star\prime}\Omega h^{\star}
=\frac{395643}{6246400},                                \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
\Gamma
=\frac{b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^2}{K}
=\frac{27}{15616}
=\frac{6663}{102400}-\frac{395643}{6246400}.            \tag{8}
\]
The covariance identity for \(Z\) makes the first expression in (7) \(\operatorname{Var}(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}Z)\); the canonical-gradient theorem makes the second \(V^{\star}\). Finally,
\[
\frac{\Gamma}{V^{\star}}
=\frac{3600}{131881}
\approx0.0272973,
\]
which is approximately \(2.73\) percent.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(C\) be finite. Under independent sampling across cohorts, i.i.d. sampling within each cohort, \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\), and \(\mathbb E_P\|Y_g\|_2^2<\infty\), the stacked cohort sample means satisfy
\[
\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Omega),
\qquad
\Omega=\Pi\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g/p_g)\Pi^{\prime}.
\]

added_lemmas.statement: In a differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment with closed score tangent space \(\mathcal T_P\), if the pathwise derivative of a scalar parameter \(\theta\) is represented on \(\mathcal T_P\) by \(\phi^{\star}\in\mathcal T_P\), then \(\phi^{\star}\) is the canonical gradient; every regular estimator has an asymptotic convolution distribution and, whenever its asymptotic variance exists, that variance is at least \(\mathbb E_P[(\phi^{\star})^2]=V^{\star}\).

source.locator: Sections 2--3, tangent-space projection and semiparametric efficiency bound

attestation.note: Stable DOI supplied because no verbatim source transcription was available; the consumer proof derives the model-specific Riesz representative and uses the cited result only for the regular-estimator lower bound.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), relative to the explicitly mean-differentiable differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment \(\mathcal T_P\), the canonical gradient is \(\phi^{\star}=h^{\star\prime}Z\), and every regular estimator of \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\) has asymptotic variance at least \(V^{\star}\).
proposed.justification: The tangent equality converts the rank-one mean manifold into a sharp semiparametric lower bound rather than a formal generalized-method-of-moments projection.
proposed.gap: Chamberlain (1987) and Newey (1990) provide projection machinery, while Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2) provides no tangent experiment or efficiency bound for the proportional ratio.
proposed.consumer: The bound is the precision benchmark needed to assess PPML inference in the regional-trade-agreement and treaty applications.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the cited regular-estimator information bound into the proof spine.

proposed.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), on \(\mathcal E_N\) the fixed-target-weight cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator obeys \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})=h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)+o_P(1)\), with asymptotic variance \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\).
proposed.justification: This differentiates the cohort-mean comparator defined in the core and identifies the exact coefficient whose cycle projection governs its efficiency loss.
proposed.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14) instead fits untreated individual-observation fixed effects and aggregates individual counterfactual predictions; neither that paper nor Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3) provides this cohort-mean influence expansion under arbitrary within-unit covariance.
proposed.consumer: The expansion lets analysts compute the cohort-mean estimator's variance and its distance from the canonical bound without conflating it with an individual fixed-effects procedure.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the cited fixed-strata central limit theorem into the proof spine.

proposed.statement: The covariance-weighted cycle estimator satisfies \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\phi_i^{\star}+o_P(1)\) and attains \(V^{\star}\) pointwise over \(\mathcal M_4\).
proposed.justification: Attainment turns the information bound into an implementable precision correction based only on cohort means and within-cohort covariances.
proposed.gap: Roth and Sant'Anna (2023, Proposition 2.1) optimize design-based additive estimators within a class; this result attains the superpopulation semiparametric bound for a nonlinear proportional target.
proposed.consumer: Applied users obtain an analytic alternative to unit-bootstrap inference for the cohort-mean PPML benchmark in fixed-horizon panels.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the cited fixed-strata central limit theorem into the feasible estimator's asymptotic-linear proof spine.

proposed.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), \(\widehat V\to_PV^{\star}\), \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})/\sqrt{\widehat V}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(\Pr_P\{\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\in[\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V/N}]\}\to1-\alpha\).
proposed.justification: Pointwise studentization completes the estimator contribution without claiming unsupported uniform inference over tail-escaping laws.
proposed.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed page 21) recommends a panel bootstrap, while the proposed efficient correction has no published analytic Wald theory.
proposed.consumer: The result yields directly reportable confidence intervals for proportional treatment effects under arbitrary within-unit dependence.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the cited fixed-strata central limit theorem into the studentization proof spine.

proposed.statement: For every fixed interior mean \(m\) with \(q>0\), the family \(P_{\rho}\) has mean \(m\), belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\), satisfies \(b_{\mathrm{cyc}}(x)=-B^{-1}D_{\mu}^{-1}x\) and \(K(x)=K_0\), and therefore obeys \(\Gamma(x)=B^{-2}x^{\prime}D_{\mu}^{-1}K_0^{-1}D_{\mu}^{-1}x>0\) for every nonzero admissible \(x\). Moreover \(\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma_0,\delta_0)\subset\mathcal L(m)\), and the explicitly chosen \(x_0\) and \(\eta_0\) satisfy \(\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma(x_0),\eta_0)\subset\mathcal L(m)\) with \(\Gamma>0\) throughout that ambient open ball.
proposed.justification: Support-preserving realizability shows that strict inefficiency is robust and not an artifact of perturbing an impossible covariance matrix.
proposed.gap: The rank-one completion and additive efficient-DiD literatures do not construct a legal nonnegative fixed-support family with an exact positive-definite cohort-mean PPML loss form.
proposed.consumer: The family supplies calibrated stress tests and interpretable variance-loss directions for cohort-mean proportional PPML applications.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the weighted-cycle rank result used to prove positive definiteness of the realized cycle Gram.

proposed.statement: Fix \(m\) and \(p\). The cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator is semiparametrically efficient for \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\) at every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\) satisfying \(\mathbb E_PY=m\) if and only if \(q=0\); when \(q>0\), its efficient covariance laws are exactly \(\mathcal L(m)\cap\ker(\mathcal L_m)\), where \(\mathcal L_m:\mathcal A_{\Sigma}\to\mathbb R^q\) has rank \(q\), and \(\|b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_2^2/\lambda_{\max}(K)\le\Gamma\le\|b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_2^2/\lambda_{\min}(K)\). This strictly sharpens Ciani and Fisher's printed-page-7, Section 3.1 observation and Appendix B simulation evidence that PPML may fail to be most efficient by giving necessity, sufficiency, and codimension for the stated cohort-mean estimator.
proposed.justification: This is the topology-level kernel: cycles are necessary and sufficient for covariance laws on which feasible precision improvement exists.
proposed.gap: Ciani and Fisher (2019, printed page 7, Section 3.1) state that PPML may fail to be the most efficient estimator, with the corresponding efficiency-loss simulations in Appendix B; Moreau--Kastler (2025, equations 3.13--3.14) and Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3) study distinct individual-level imputation procedures. None gives an acyclic if-and-only-if frontier or an exact codimension count for the cohort-mean rank-one estimator.
proposed.consumer: The theorem tells analysts in the Nagengast--Yotov and Menkhoff--Miethe settings exactly when the transparent cohort-mean PPML benchmark is universally precision-optimal before moving to richer individual-level specifications.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cohort-mean linearization and cycle-loss definition used in the estimator-efficiency and spectral-loss steps.

proposed.statement:
If \(q=0\), then \(R\) has no columns, \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}\), \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\), and \(\Gamma=0\). Within the maintained model, the canonical acyclic support \(C=\{2,\infty\}\) has \(q=0\) for every fixed \(T\ge3\), and on \(\mathcal E_N\),
\[
\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}
=\frac{\sum_{t=2}^T\overline Y_{2t}}
{\overline Y_{21}\sum_{t=2}^T
(\overline Y_{\infty t}/\overline Y_{\infty1})}-1.
\]
proposed.justification: The reduction checks inside the maintained \(T\ge3\) model that the cycle correction vanishes and that cohort-mean PPML becomes an explicit multi-post multiplicative ratio.
proposed.gap: Ciani and Fisher (2019) establish the canonical two-period multiplicative DiD ratio; this proposition gives the admissible fixed-\(T\), \(T\ge3\), acyclic analogue that pools all post-adoption cells.
proposed.consumer: Users with one treated cohort and a never-treated cohort can compute the multi-post proportional effect directly and omit covariance-cycle estimation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the primitive characterization and loss definition used for the empty-cycle conclusions.

proposed.statement: In \(\mathsf E_3\), all realized outcomes are positive, \(q=1\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}=1/2\), \(V^{\star}=395643/6246400\), \(\operatorname{Var}(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}Z)=6663/102400\), and \(\Gamma=27/15616\); hence the cohort-mean PPML variance exceeds the bound by approximately \(2.73\) percent of \(V^{\star}\).
proposed.justification: The exact rational witness makes the cohort-mean PPML topology loss quantitatively auditable in the smallest cyclic staggered panel.
proposed.gap: Published multiplicative DiD examples do not report this PTT-specific canonical bound and exact cycle loss for a legal nonnegative covariance law.
proposed.consumer: The exhibit provides a reproducible calibration for implementations of the cycle correction.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A growing-dimensional theorem requires a specified triangular-array model for \(T_N\), \(q_N\), cohort shares, graph spectra, tail envelopes, and a concrete spectral regularization rule; the frozen handle does not define these objects or an ordering under which one set of conditions could be called weakest.
open_obligations.obstruction: Pointwise finite fourth moments at each fixed law do not control the smallest nonzero eigenvalues of \(K_N\), the operator error of \(\widehat K_N\), the high-dimensional cycle-score approximation, or studentization uniformly as \(q_N\) grows. Assuming those conclusions would assume the crux, while the fixed-horizon core supplies no triangular-array class from which to derive them.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-dimensional spectral projection was decomposed into retained-cycle stochastic error and discarded-loading bias. Closing either term for increasing \(q_N\) needs, respectively, a uniform self-normalized central limit condition and quantitative eigenvalue/loading decay assumptions not present in the frozen core.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every fixed \(T\) and fixed \(q\), the proved expansion is
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})
=
\{h_{\mathrm{CM}}-R(R^{\prime}\Omega R)^{-1}
R^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\}^{\prime}
\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)+o_P(1),
\]
with consistent studentization. This establishes the complete fixed-dimensional boundary case but does not determine a growing-\(q\) regularization frontier.
